relations.note: Itomi Pavá literally denotes Pavá’s son or children and celestial emissaries.
Kashíri fathers the Sun, making Pavá’s children his indirect descendants.

relations.myth: Missionary identification of the returning celestial savior
relations.note: Missionaries equated the true Amachegua or returning Son of Pavá with Christ.
relations.source: Sala diary; Stahl and Bodley materials

relations.note: Mission discourse translated Son of Pavá as Son of God.
relations.source: Brown and Fernández, War of Shadows

relations.myth: The celestial helper descends to aid Asháninka fighters
relations.note: Amachénga and Itomi Pavá overlap as returning celestial-helper categories, though exact equivalence remains disputed.

relations.myth: The killed Inca survives and will return
relations.note: Some Asháninka narratives explicitly identify the killed and returning Inca as Itomi Pavá.

other_aliases: Juan Santos Huayna Cápac Apu Inca
relations.myth: The rebel survives or reincarnates as returning savior
relations.note: Later traditions identify Juan Santos as a manifestation or predecessor of Itomi Pavá.
relations.source: Brown and Fernández, War of Shadows

relations.myth: Divine warrior preserving the Juan Santos tradition
relations.note: Scholarly reconstruction tentatively connects Sacaramentaro through Juan Santos with Itomi Pavá.
A skeptic warned that the supposed Itomi Pavá might instead be a deceptive kamári.
relations.source: Brown and Fernández, War of Shadows

relations.myth: Adventist preaching prompts expectations of immediate celestial renewal
relations.note: Some followers identified Stahl or his mission station with the expected divine agent.
relations.source: Bodley materials summarized by Brown and Fernández

relations.myth: Followers journey to Bulner’s Río Ene mission
relations.note: Some Asháninka and Nomatsiguenga hailed Bulner as Itomi Pavá, then repudiated the identification.

relations.myth: Ernesto recognizes the MIR commander as Son of the Sun
relations.note: Shaman Ernesto Andrés identified Lobatón as Itomi Pavá, mobilizing supporters before catastrophic disconfirmation.
relations.source: Brown and Fernández, War of Shadows

relations.myth: White stranger claims Father Sun sent him
relations.note: Reyna retrospectively identified the 1888 Amachengua claimant with Fitzcarrald; the equation remains unproven.
relations.source: Reyna, Fitzcarraldo, el rey del caucho
